item.title: Caleb Abroad: Day 5 and some 6
item.description:
Well well, the expected has finally occured - I missed a day. A full refund, for your bitter disappointment, is available upon request.

Berlin

This post’s title is a lie, as we actually need to start on the evening of Day 4, the last post ending with my train’s arrival.

It was clear from the get-go that the Sunflower was a different kind of hostel than the Madhouse. It still has a hip, indie vibe, but is both bigger and less thrown-together, for lack of a better phrase. The Madhouse felt like a big house that a group of friends lived in, where you could join in on the peripherary of their circle for a while; the Sunflower is a cool, cheap hotel where you share a room with other people. That’s the best way I can explain. As will become clear, I far prefer this one.

item.title: Caleb Abroad: Day 4
item.description:
Previous post

Up and out

I woke up with a runny nose and a vague sort of sadness. The runny nose was a touch of some kind of cold, that would hang around for most of the day (or the second day of a hangover? Surely not…); the sadness was that it was time to leave Prague, and through a combination of bad luck and ill judgement I’d wasted a lot of the time I’d had there. I hadn’t read as much as I’d planned, hadn’t seen as much as I should, hadn’t had as good a time as I’d hoped. I’d met more people than I’d expected to, sure, and they’d all been friendly. But none of these connections had been deep, and most fellow travellers had had this peculiar quality behind their friendliness, this lack of solidity, almost. So many introductions and conversations and cultural comparisons, and I felt like I’d managed to meet only about two actual, real people. Lying in my bunk, light snoring echoing all about me, and the ambience of a busy street floating in through the window, feeling lonely and tired.

item.title: Caleb Abroad: Day 3
item.description:
Previous post

Wednesday’s first moments of consciousness are hard to pinpoint. As I recall, I awoke a few times that morning, and each time had the same moment of wondering why I was lying on my back (I’m almost exclusively a side-sleeper), fully-clothed, mouth dry as the Sahara, and each time I’d sink back into the mind’s deep darkness again. However many times this played out, when I finally came-to on a more permanent basis I had enough power trickling through my crusted brain to wonder at each of these things again, and what’s more, to try to recall how it was that I got to my bed to begin with.

item.title: Caleb Abroad: Day 1
item.description:
Beginning

Hello hello, and welcome back! Yes, it has been a little while hasn’t it - ignore the cobwebs, if you can, this place may be dusty but it’s still home…

I’ve had quite the haitus from writing. Truth be told, I’ve had quite the haitus from quite a number of things - this last year has been interesting, in a few ways.

Actually scratch that (why do I start acting all aloof when I write blog posts?), it was just really fucking hard. I came within inches of quitting my job (and with it, my degree), I watched as a community I loved got damaged by the ego of someone who was supposed to care for it, I tried to do what I thought was right and lost a friend and mentor in the process. And even after I left that place and my responsibility to it, life found a way to still be hard.

item.title: The Truth
item.description:
Friends, I have something to tell you. All of you. I take no pleasure in revealing it, but there are some things which can’t be kept hidden. I’ve kept this from you all. But I am not here to make excuses, or to even explain myself. I just want to tell the truth.

And there’s a lot to tell, too much for this website’s normal post format to take. I’m serious, when I finally compiled it all into something I was happy with (well, not happy per se, but… you know what I mean), the budget server I and Adrianne share didn’t have enough space on its drive.

item.title: Assignment season strikes again
item.description:
Just when the seasonal depression lifts, assignment season swoops in to replace it. When will it end?

In reality, it ends in about 10 days for me. But for now, I’d like to be dramatic about it.

And why is it too that the weather is absolutely amazing when you’re studying but it rains as soon as you finish your last exam? These are the questions that need to be asked. I’m not sure to whom, but I’m pretty angry about it.

item.title: bad weather for ducks
item.description:
What a suddenly beautiful day today is! I sat out for a good two hours this afternoon, photosynthesizing to my hearts content. Does you wonders, sunlight. Helps you forget your woes, like the vicious rotting-egg-stink that will not lift from your house’s kitchen. The less said of it the better.

I made my triumphant return to the gym today. And by triumphant, I mean that I really didn’t want to, and I’d slept in so I felt groggy, and since it’s been a month since I last went I had to drop my weights on several exercises and felt embarrassed despite the fact that no one around me knew what weight I’d been doing before anyway…

item.title: Some Good News (not from me)
item.description:
The news is never really very happy, is it? As in THE news, not just news. Most of the time, news is in the news because it’s bad news. This fact is quite depressing.

So today I’d like to just share some good news. Like your daily news update, but only good stuff.

For a start, the world record for the longest plank has been beaten by a 58-year-old grandmother of 12. DonnaJean Wilde managed to plank for 4.5 hours. How crazy is that? If I did a minute of planking, I would think I’m unstoppable. DonnaJean is out here showing us all up. A super-granny, if you will. That’s some pretty happy news.

item.title: Blog, blog, the rattlin’ blog
item.description:
Missed me?

No that’s alright you don’t have to answer that.

Been a little while, hasn’t it? I can only apologize. And provide Adrianne with, what at the point must surely be, a lifetime supply of drinks.

I won’t go into why this little absence started initially, other than to say that group projects suck.

I’m actually in the Netherlands as I write this, in Rotterdam. It’s been a weird family holiday, not just because it’s been a minute since we did this, all five of us. It’s simply a weird time of year for all of us to be here, Mom and Dad and with the work they needed to be doing while we prepared for it, and I with the work I s_till_ need to be doing even during it.

item.title: Cindy
item.description:
Well it’s been a while. Nice to meet again. 

It’s been a weird few weeks. As a first post back, I just want to dedicate it to my little westie Cindy who passed away last week. She was truly the best dog ever. She had a long and full life at 15 years old so I’m just very thankful for how long we had with her. 

Cindy had a pretty wild last day. She ate 3 pupcakes and had her first puppuccino. She went on her last walk, which didn’t last very long but she got to sniff a lot of patches of grass. And we had lots and lots of cuddles to top it all off.

item.title: The Water We Swim In
item.description:
I have been busy this week.

What a stock phrase that is, and for most of you not at all unusual, but it is for me. I am not used to being busy. I am not used to doing a great many things at any time. I also have a terrible habit of praying for specific things and forgetting that I did, and I have a sinking feeling that a month or two ago I asked God that I might be stretched more than I have been recently. Well whether I asked for that or not, it’s happening alright. And it’s both good and bad.

item.title: Lent
item.description:
Lent this year has come up really suddenly. It’s like one minute I was talking about all the things I wanted to do with Lent and the next I’m actually having to do them. Imagine that.

Honestly, I feel a lot less willing to do anything for Lent this year. Last year was the first time I’d actually done something for it and I really appreciated it. This year, I just don’t really want to give anything up. But I’m doing it anyway because I feel like I should. I know I’ll appreciate it a lot more in like March but 4 days in, I’m not loving life.

item.title: How does God speak to us?
item.description:
I’ve kinda struggled with this recently. I grew up in a pretty traditional Christian home so I really hadn’t thought about it much. I thought that God only spoke through the words written in His word, the Bible.

But recently I’ve just come to the sorta realisation that God communicates with us in loads of ways. When i say realisation, i mean that God keeps speaking to me and i keep ignoring it. I keep telling myself that it’s not God, it’s just a coincidence, or it’s just my mind making it up, or it’s just lucky that that specific person knew exactly what i needed to hear and said it to me.

item.title: ”Add title”
item.description:
My mind is having many thoughts. Not many useful ones as I try to come up with a topic to write about this week. But many thoughts are occurring.

I guess the main thought that I’m having is that I have no thoughts. But then again, that is a thought. Therefore, I do have thoughts, just not ones that I want to have.

As Descartes once described it “I think therefore I am”. But I’m not questioning my existence; I’m just questioning my ability to write anything of substance. Is this substantial? Is what I’m writing of any substance?

item.title: thinkful thoughts
item.description:
i have many thoughts today. i think, in fact, that the thoughts might have thoughts themselves. here, have three of them:

it’s so easy to believe that focus will come to us (or become us) when we need it, as we sit down at out desk/steering wheel/reading chair, that our brains will shift gear all by themselves. this is sometimes so, with habit (Pavlov but with the scent of coffee, a particular view) or stress (the deep sinking sensation as you consider Newton’s formulae applied to a 2-tonne vehicle at speed). but focus sometimes needs to be a choice we make, a division of our strength we make for ourselves. what a tricky thing it can be, though, the balance between trusting our mind to work out a course without our knowing, and grabbing it with both hands to set it straight.

item.title: Driving and I
item.description: I awoke the same way I wake up every morning – groggily, reluctantly, mind entirely absent of anything except how cold and bright and horrible the whole world outside the bed is, my internal awareness ignorant of anything except how annoyed I feel. But the door had been opened and the light streaming in forced more of my mind to come to life, and once the fog of tired malaise had lifted enough for solid thought to form beneath it, the first of these lit up my whole brain like some damned firecracker.

item.description:
So as I said last week, I went on a skiing trip for the first time. It was so so fun and I really enjoyed it and I would recommend it to everyone. However, as always, I did embarrass myself a few times. So here’s a run down of my most embarrassing moments as a professional skier.

item.description:
Well hello there. 

I’m writing this on the plane home from Austria. Last week, i mighttttt have forgotten to put up a new post because we were travelling for most of that day. I’m sure everyone was devastated to miss it. 

Anyway, i hope everyone had a lovely Christmas and a happy new year!! I feel like Christmas is still going, like the Christmas spirit has been here for longer this year. I love Christmas so I’m pretty happy about that. 
But now that I’m heading home, i think it’s time to go back to reality; take the Christmas tree down and heal from the many bruises that I’ve acquired whilst skiing.

item.title: Caleb’s End Of Year List (Part One)

item.title: Happy Christmas
item.description:
Today’s post from me is just a little Happy Christmas. We’ve made it to the end of the year and now we get to eat loads of good food and rot on the sofa for a while. Well done us.

Whether Christmas for you is usually a happy time or is usually a tough time, I really pray that God blesses you this Christmas. And throughout all of the chaos and busyness that the season brings, I hope you’re able to find peace and relaxation.

item.title: Conversing
item.description:
I have a strange relationship with conversations.

Conversations are strange beasties, and they come in many shapes and sizes. Some are small and quick, little insects of interaction. “Hey, how’s it going?” “Oh fine, I’m just off to an appointment” “Oh nice, well see you later” “See you later”. There’s no thinking needed to have a conversation like this. You can have them with someone you barely know or someone you love (although the tone will likely be different).

item.title: Is it ever possible to really relax?
item.description:
Hi there. It’s been a long week. Finished my last assignment yesterday and thought yay i can relax now!

But what does relaxing actually mean? Is it watching a tv show or hanging out with your friends or going out with family or doing some Christmas shopping maybe? Because I’ve found that while I enjoy all of these things, they haven’t helped me to actually relax.

So then to relax maybe I need to just completely turn my brain off. How is that possible? Sure i can watch a movie or tv show or knit or read but all of it still feels like I’m doing a task. So how do I switch my brain off?

item.title: A review of Unreal Unearth by Hozier
item.description:
So Hozier put out a new album in August called Unreal Unearth. I’m not particularly a big fan of Hozier; I fiercely resisted his music because I wanted to believe that I’m not a basic white girl. But this album has got a hold on me.

I heard of the album around the time that it came out, but was very quickly put off by the horrific cover art. If you haven’t seen it, prepare yourself before viewing. It might be the worst album cover I’ve ever seen.

item.title: Thanksgiving
item.description:
So on Thursday we celebrated Thanksgiving. Yeah it’s an American tradition but I guess it’s a still good reminder to be thankful for the little things.

As a Christian, giving thanks for what God’s given me is important. So I decided to turn to the Bible and see what God says about giving thanks.

  • 1 Thessalonians 5 v. 18 – In everything give thanks; for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus for you.
  • Philippians 4 v. 6 – Be anxious for nothing, but in everything by prayer and supplication, with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God.
  • Psalms 100 v. 4 – Enter into His gates with thanksgiving, and into His courts with praise. Be thankful to Him, and bless His name.

God calls us to be thankful in all circumstances. This is pretty difficult. Sometimes we feel like we have very little to be thankful for. But we can always be thankful that our God in heaven loves us and he understands when we find it difficult to thank Him.

item.title: A Break
item.description:
Hello avid readers. This week me and Adrianne are off to the wilds of Newcastle for a weekend away and we figured it was a good point, after ten posts each, for a lil break.

We know many of you won’t know what to do with your mid-afternoon without us, so here are some suggestions for how to fill the oatb-less void. We hope they’ll enrich your day and have you come back next week knowing more of yourself and the world than before.

item.title: On Writing
item.description:
A bright summers day in a small classroom. Children are scribbling on worksheets while babbling to each-other about football or their brother or how far they can kick either object. Not much work is getting done, but it’s late in the year so no one really minds. The teacher sure doesn’t, and is sitting absent-mindedly marking something or other, or maybe she too is doodling aimlessly.

She looks up to a boy standing politely beside her desk. He beams shyly and waves a stack of pages. Each is covered in a dense scrawl of bad joint-up handwriting. 07/05/2015 is written in the margin, like it’s a homework. He says it’s a story he’s written, and asks if he could read some of it to the class.

item.title: Be Still
item.description:
Be still, and know that I am God; I will be exalted among the nations, I will be exalted in the earth! ~ Psalm 46 v10

Life is so fast-paced. It’s difficult to find time to just stop and “be still”. Even when we’re taking time to relax, there’s usually something on your mind that’s keeping you from getting the mental rest that you need.

This verse is a reminder that God is in control, even in those moments when you feel like your mind can’t rest or you’re so busy that you can’t get a minute to unwind. He is the God of all. We can be still with the knowledge that our God is a good God.

item.title: Resourcing: Part 3
item.description:
The doors opened slowly, and a full panorama of her floor filled Alice’s vision. Colours were everywhere, squiggled in strange shapes across the floor, covering the ceiling tiles in shifting patterns, and splattered across every single desk in the form of potted plants and mood-boards. Every hue known to man, she thought, must surely be on her floor.

Alice found her way to her workspace. It was colourful too, with drawings and sketches scattered so that only a few brief glimpses of desk could be made out. Cork boards were stood up all around, each holding hundreds of sticky notes and other small drawings, most of them just blobs of colour with words like “brand”, “technology” and “values” written across them. In the corner of the desk sat a stuffed bear and a framed photograph of an older woman.

item.title: Resourcing: Part 2
item.description:
Darkness. The stifled warble of deep yawning. The unsteady percussion of feet on tile floor. Curses as a lamp is reached for and not found. Hands groping out at empty space and finally finding soft linen. Curtains flung open and sharp blades of light flying inward. Anne blinked at the day she had just brought into being.

The sun shone onto the city, and the city shone back. On the streets below the last dregs of rush-hour were making their presence known with a symphony of horn and brake. Many of these pointed out of town, along a road aimed solely at a single group of buildings, which gleamed brightest of all. Even from her apartment three miles away Anne could see them clear as day, their great glass fronts glistening, opal walls so reflective they ought to come with a recommended SPF. What few birds there were chirped pleasant harmonies as they sought after what little greenery the roads and parking lots hadn’t taken. It was 9:30.

item.title: Bread of the banana kind

item.title: Procrasto-paralysis
item.description:
Have you ever been going about your day, loafing around, walking somewhere, when suddenly your stomach falls and there’s a weird itching thought in the back of your mind:

“There’s something I should be doing right now”.

And you don’t have an inkling what that thing is, but it feels important. So you think, try to pull it out of whatever recess of your mind it’s hiding in, because if it’s important then it needs doing. You need to go get it done.

item.title: Gregory Alan Isakov’s new album
item.description:

item.title: Resourcing: Part One
item.description:
There’s a place way out in the wild, far from any town, where the trees grow taller and stronger than anywhere else. Life thrives under their boughs: caterpillars and ants, rabbits and badgers, hawthorn and honeysuckle. They say nature has taken back what is hers. They say no-one has gone there in decades.

But if you were to go there, hacking through the underbrush,if you dug a little here and there, deep below the canopy and the ferns and the grass, you’d find concrete and steel jutting out from the earth. Dig a little deeper and you’d find the remains of walls and lampposts. Further still and roads, tunnels and underground car parks would rise up from beneath your feet.

item.title: Apology
item.description:
I am sorry, blog. From day one I haven’t treated you right. I promised you I’d give you time, spend the week honing and crafting each post to streamlined excellence. Instead I’ve banged out every one of them with an hour to go, typing with the speed and abandon of a Buzzfeed editor on crack.

I should’ve done better by you, blog. But how about this – a promise. Yes, yes, you’ve heard enough of them, I know. But this one’s airtight. A covenant. Next week I will publish a full short story. And not some weaselly little two-paragrapher either, no – a full mini-novella. How about that blog? Sound good? Alright you don’t believe me. But a promise is a promise. And I will deliver

item.title: A review of the first week back at uni
item.description:
Well hello again. I’m back. Back in Belfast, back in uni, and back on your screen. This week was the first week back at Queen’s. It’s been a weird one. Second year is slightly more stressful than first year. Not in terms of workload. Probably just because people keep asking if it’s more stressful so I feel like I should be stressed. Don’t ask people that. Just don’t.

Anyway, the first week of uni is weird. Moving out again is fun and involves loads of socialising, and making too many cups of tea at once because literally everyone wants one, but that’s a lot for us introverts. I think I deserve some time to wrap up in my duvet and rot while watching Modern Family. I would love to have no thoughts for like an hour. I suppose that’s what Sunday afternoons are for.

item.title: On Technology
item.description:
Hello again, take a seat. How have you been? Oh really? I’ve been doing quite well myself. Just moved into my accommodation, and things are going swimmingly. I think me and my roommate are going to have to rearrange the furniture again though – his piano arrived and its dimensions were somewhat underappreciated.

I’ve been thinking about technology lately. Truth be told I think about it a lot, and not just because of what I study. The stuff’s just everywhere now, and I’ve found becoming an adult (only technically of course, everyone knows a student is just a large child with sleep deprivation) only increases the scenarios where you need your phone or your laptop to do things. Or at least, think you do.

item.title: Humble beginnings, and a poem
item.description:
Welcome to the show! You’re reading Of All The Blogs, me and my friend Adrianne’s new venture into the world of making people read stuff we write.

What sort of blog will it be, I hear you ask? Whatever we please. Each week, Saturday at 3PM, we’ll both put up a post about something. Something interesting, something personal, something long, something short.

This first post will be in that last category. I write this seated on my bedside, fingers firing as fast as I can think of words to type. I meant to labor over this post (my very first) over the whole week, to woo you prospective readers with some well-crafted opening – some grand, sweeping summary of what a blog is, who I am, where I’m at in life and where I want to go, imparting wisdom at every turn of phrase and leaving your screens oozing with dry wit and clever writing.

item.title: First impressions
item.description:
Hi. I’m Adrianne. This is my first post.

As I’ve been thinking of what I want this first post to be, I’ve had a lot of writer’s block. Wanting to make a good first impression has been holding me back. So that got me thinking about how we deal with making first impressions. For me, I find that meeting new people comes with a lot of nervousness and apprehension. While some people thrive off of making new friends, some of us are just more comfortable staying in our own bubble of the people who already know us.

item.title: About
item.description:
Of all the blogs, you chose this one?

Welcome to our blog! We are two students from Belfast who have lots of thoughts about lots of things that we’d like to share. Here you’ll find us writing weekly (hopefully) about many different topics that we’re interested in. This ranges from politics to programming, pop culture to poetry, and pets to predestination.

Please get in touch via our emails (in the contact section) if you’d like to discuss anything that we write about; we’d love to chat!
